rationale.scope: Budgets were fixed from documented guarantees and peer ceilings before any Events capacity measurement; they are never tuned to an observed result. docs/events/README.md publishes no throughput or p99 numbers, so every ceiling is inherited from a peer path that contains or resembles the Events hot path.
rationale.workload: The documented hot path is a caller-transaction append (one stream lock, one duplicate lookup, one bulk insert, one head update; README 'Batch cost'), bounded reads, and leased pull-based catch-up into the inbox. Eight tenants x four streams keep appenders on distinct streams (README: one stream deliberately serializes writers). 1 KiB seeded high-entropy payloads are well inside the 1 MiB event and 8 MiB batch limits.
rationale.durationAndRepeats: Two clean exact-candidate runs of 30 minutes each, the same minimum every other expansion capacity gate (Search, Edge, Jobs, Documents, Projections) requires.
rationale.offeredRates: Appenders offer 40 transactions/s (160 events/s), readers 40/s and consumers 80 batches/s. Projections qualifies 20 business commits/s that each contain one Events append, and Jobs 20 completions/s; the Events component must sustain at least twice that composite rate.
rationale.minimumAcceptedPerSecond: 95% of each fixed offered rate: Edge's maximumSkippedFraction of 0.05 is the strictest peer schedule-skip ceiling, and Events has no admission control that may reject.
rationale.maximumRejectedFractionAndErrors: Zero. PostgreSqlEventStore has no backpressure rejection; any exception is an error, and invariant violations abort the run.
rationale.append.maximumP99Milliseconds: 500 ms: an append is one durable transaction, so it inherits the Documents single-document save ceiling (maximumSaveP99Milliseconds 500). It is stricter than the Projections business-commit ceiling (1000 ms), which contains an Events append plus projection work.
rationale.read.maximumP99Milliseconds: 500 ms: a bounded indexed read of at most 64 events must not be slower than the cheapest peer durable write ceiling (Documents save, 500 ms).
rationale.replay.maximumP99Milliseconds: 1000 ms: one catch-up batch is one store-owned transaction that runs the handler, inbox inserts and checkpoint advance for up to 256 events, the same shape as the Projections business commit (maximumCommitP99Milliseconds 1000).
rationale.delivery.maximumP99Milliseconds: 2000 ms commit-to-checkpoint: Projections bounds commit-to-inbox delivery at maximumInboxP99Milliseconds 2000; pull-based Events catch-up must deliver no slower.
rationale.replayDrainSeconds: 60 s: Projections capacity bounds post-offer drain at maximumDrainSeconds 60.
rationale.acceptedEvents.minimumPerSecond: 152 events/s = 4 events x 38 accepted append transactions/s.
rationale.maximumOwnedGrowthBytesPerUnit: 4096 bytes per accepted event = 4 x payloadBytes. README 'Retention' documents linear growth with event count (identity, stream, checkpoint and inbox rows are kept; retention is off by default); the payload is stored once in the outbox, and the 4x factor bounds identity, inbox and index amplification.
rationale.maximumWalBytesPerUnit: 16384 bytes per accepted event. Jobs admits 65536 bytes of cluster WAL per accepted job across four durable row transitions (enqueue, claim, complete, prune), i.e. 16 KiB per durable transition; an accepted event is one outbox/identity insert plus one inbox insert.
rationale.maximumOwnedRelationBytes: 2 GiB: the Projections capacity owned-storage ceiling, which already includes its Events outbox.
rationale.maximumDatabaseBytes: 8 GiB: the Search and Documents whole-database ceiling.
